title: Indian summer: The BRICS summit and warming New Delhi-Beijing relations – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: At the New Delhi BRICS summit, Xi Jinping's first India visit in over six years showcased Sino-Indian normalisation that is tactical rather than a realignment — but India is opening to Chinese investment in manufacturing and climate tech, a warning that Europe must accelerate EU-India tech, defence and research ties or lose ground to Beijing.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping's visit to the September 2026 BRICS summit in New Delhi was his first trip to India in more than six years, the latest step in Sino-Indian normalisation after a sustained period of tension.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Marker of reduced India-China border/political risk premium.
insights.locator: The BRICS summit concluded in New Delhi

insights.claim: New Delhi's normalisation with Beijing over the past year looks more like tactical de-escalation than a geopolitical realignment; India still views China as a security threat.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Don't extrapolate thaw into full strategic convergence; security-sensitive sectors stay closed to China.
insights.quote: looks like more of a tactical de-escalation than a realignment

insights.claim: India has begun agreeing measures giving Chinese investment greater access to its manufacturing and climate-technology sectors, both important for India's development.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Chinese capital into Indian manufacturing/clean-tech could compress costs for Indian producers and compete with Western suppliers for Indian market share.

insights.claim: If India cannot source technology and capital from European partners, it will source them from China even while remaining suspicious of Beijing on security grounds.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Speed of EU capital/tech offers to India determines whether Chinese suppliers capture India's manufacturing and clean-tech build-out.
insights.quote: If India cannot source technology and capital from partners in Europe, it will seek to do so from China

insights.claim: Modi has worked to prevent BRICS from becoming a purely anti-Western vehicle because that would run against India's interests in deeper ties with Brussels and Washington.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: India acts as a brake on BRICS de-dollarisation/anti-Western initiatives.
insights.locator: New Delhi continues to view Beijing

insights.claim: BRICS has grown from its original five to eleven members including Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, but is internally divided (e.g. both Iran and the UAE are members) and the 2026 summit produced only a limited declaration with vague cooperation promises.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Low odds of coordinated BRICS economic action; treat summit rhetoric as noise.
insights.locator: India supported moves at the 2023 BRICS summit

insights.claim: The EU and India signed a landmark free-trade agreement in New Delhi in January 2026 alongside a new security and defence partnership, aiming to expand cooperation on semiconductors, AI and clean-tech supply chains.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: EU-India FTA implementation is a tailwind for European exporters and India-based supply-chain diversification plays.
insights.locator: The EU and India signed a landmark

insights.claim: Ahead of Modi's expected Brussels visit, the EU should upgrade the Trade and Technology Council to drive AI cooperation, advance defence and security cooperation and speed India's accession to Horizon Europe.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Watch Modi's Brussels visit for TTC/AI and Horizon Europe deliverables as signals of EU-India tech alignment.
insights.locator: Ahead of Modi’s anticipated visit to Brussels

insights.claim: India's bilateral agreements with China, including on the BRICS sidelines, show the EU cannot take the mutual benefits of closer EU-India ties for granted.
insights.speaker: James Crabtree
insights.so_what: Counter to the consensus that the EU-India FTA locks in India's Western tilt.
insights.quote: the EU must not take the mutual benefits of closer ties for granted
